newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power holds steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power holds steady to higher.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West were steady to higher Wednesday with continued strength from some cold weather and strong natural gas prices, brokers and marketers said.
"We're still seeing some pretty good demand with some (generation) units out," said one Mid-West power trader.
Temperatures in the northern areas were reaching highs in the mid-20s degrees Fahrenheit Wednesday.
Detroit Edison's 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power plant in Monroe County, Mich., could restart as soon as Friday following a repair outage, the company said Wednesday.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power deals for Thursday delivery were pegged steady to higher at $26.00-28.50 from $25.00-27.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Tuesday, the brokers and marketers said.
Peak wholesale power was said to be relatively scarce in states like Minnesota and the Dakotas with utilities reluctant to part with spot power.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Thursday delivery was pegged steady to lower at $22.50-24.50 from $23.00-25.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday delivery were assessed steady at $21.00-23.00, although a few deals late in the day were reported as high as $25.00 per MWh.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
January and February peak ECAR prices were notionally pegged steady at $23.40-23.80 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were talked steady at $20.00-22.00 in the north of the region, while prices in southern SPP were pegged at $24.00-26.00 per MWh.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area.
January/February peak SPP power was pegged steady at $25.75-26.25 per MWh on Monday, the sources said.
